items.stem: A RAG answer is wrong even though the correct passage was retrieved into context. Where is the fault most likely?

options.text: In generation (the model mis-used the available context)
options.rationale: Correct: if the right context was retrieved, the failure lies in how the answer was generated.
Retrieval succeeded here, so it is not the fault.
A network issue is not indicated by this symptom.
The symptom points to generation, not input spelling.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about evaluating a RAG system are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Retrieval quality and answer quality should be measured separately
options.rationale: Correct: separating them lets you locate the fault.

options.text: Answer grounding checks whether claims are supported by retrieved context
options.rationale: Correct: grounding/faithfulness measures support in the context.

options.text: A fluent answer is proof it is faithful to the sources
options.rationale: Fluency is not evidence of faithfulness.

options.text: One accuracy number fully describes retrieval quality
options.rationale: Retrieval needs measures like recall and precision, not a single number.

items.explanation: Correct: separating them lets you locate the fault.

items.stem: Which measure captures how many of the relevant passages were successfully retrieved?

options.rationale: Correct: recall measures the fraction of relevant items that were retrieved.
Latency measures speed, not relevance coverage.
Cost is unrelated to retrieval coverage.
Uptime measures availability, not retrieval coverage.

items.explanation: Correct: recall measures the fraction of relevant items that were retrieved.
